### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **12** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**5** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/client-sdk.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface), FlowFailureDetails (symbol, a top-level type))_
- `content/docs/api/declarative-endpoints.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface), /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/error-handling.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface AutomationResult))_
- `content/docs/protocol/kernel/http-protocol.mdx`  _(via /api/v1/automation/:name/trigger (route, a path literal in a comment on a changed line; bridged from symbol TriggerFlowResponseSchema — its route source's handler names it))_

⛔ **5** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface), userMessage (symbol, a field of interface AutomationResult))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-3.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-4.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface AutomationResult))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via AutomationResult (symbol, a top-level interface))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/index.mdx`  _(via userMessage (symbol, a field of interface AutomationResult))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **6** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts`, `packages/spec/api-surface/api.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/api.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **149** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `6bf75f27ef21ad1b6f7bb571ec9ceda5de665fd6` — the merge of head `22786c992e928af6c43ca807998408adb52add4e` into base `3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 6bf75f27ef21ad1b6f7bb571ec9ceda5de665fd6 && git checkout 6bf75f27ef21ad1b6f7bb571ec9ceda5de665fd6
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f 22786c992e928af6c43ca807998408adb52add4e && git checkout -B drift-repro 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f && git merge --no-ff 22786c992e928af6c43ca807998408adb52add4e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3b3830ca223eaea7875babb155e47eebbcd0300f` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `22786c992e928af6c43ca807998408adb52add4e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/spec/src/api/contract.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/api/error-code-ledger.zod.ts, packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts, packages/runtime/src/actions-flow-dispatch-status.test.ts, packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts, packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.test.ts

### ① Derived judgments

Read against card #24996 (ruling B′ on #24914, decision `6297041774`, batch #379 item 5), #9378 `5321043983`, #9585 `5339708379`, and the net three-dot diff of `22786c992e` against `main` (13 files).

1. **`AutomationResult` gains `userMessage?` and `innerRefusal?`** — `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts:551-580`. The card locates `AutomationResult` at `automation/flow.zod.ts:1085`; those lines are `FlowSchema`'s authored `successMessage`/`errorMessage` (flow-definition keys, not the run result). The dev's premise correction is right: the interface the ruling names lives in `contracts/automation-service.ts`, and its Zod mirror is `TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data`. `flow.zod.ts` is untouched, which is the correct reading (a runtime-produced `userMessage` is not an authorable key). The `userMessage` docblock binds to `ApiErrorSchema.userMessage` semantics (`contract.zod.ts`: presence is the marking, producer opt-in at throw time, "never replaces" the diagnostic channel) — faithful to bullet 1.
2. **`TriggerFlowResponseSchema.data` mirrors both** (`automation-api.zod.ts:428-436`); the compile-time parity pin `TriggerFlowDataMatchesContract` (#13078) is untouched and still has to hold, and a second pin `FlowFailureInnerRefusalIsTheContracts` ties `FlowFailureDetails['innerRefusal']` to `AutomationResult['innerRefusal']`. Declared once, not twice: the interface imports `FlowInnerRefusal` (type-only) from the api module, so the two cannot drift.
3. **`FlowInnerRefusalSchema` — `code` is the closed `ErrorCode`.** Checked at the head: `ErrorCode` (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts:1634`, `z.enum`) is exactly what `ApiErrorSchema.code` parses against (`contract.zod.ts:29`), and `UNIQUE_VIOLATION` is a member (ledger rows at :1069, :1378, :1457). So "wire spelling" is enforced, not just described: the member accepts what a record save answers in `error.code` and refuses a driver spelling (`ER_DUP_ENTRY`, tested at `['code']`). This IS the ruling's wire spelling — `error.code` on the wire is always a closed member since #9106; an app-specific spelling rides `declaredCode`, never `error.code`. Reviewer choice 1 accepted. Consequence for #24914 (flagged below, not a defect here): the member has no `declaredCode` arm, so a hook refusal with an unregistered code must be demoted by the emitter with the same `demotedDeclaredCode` read the doors already use, and the app's own spelling is not carried inside the member. The ruling fixed the shape to `{ code, message }`, so that is within the ruling, not a loss the spec seat could have avoided without re-ruling.
4. **`FlowFailureDetailsSchema` declared once for the four doors** (`automation-api.zod.ts:584-600`): `errorMessage?`, `summary?` (`FlowRunSummarySchema`), `innerRefusal?`. Plain non-strict `z.object`, the same shape class as `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` (`:503`), so on the resume door `runId`/`status`/`repairable` parse beside these keys from one `details` object; the test proves both schemas accept each other's members. Bullet 2 is met: one declaration, four doors. Note the spec has no per-door binding of `details` schemas (the doors live in runtime), so "declared once" is the schema plus the test's four-door matrix; emission is #24914's, as the card says.
5. **`AutomationResult.code` unchanged and closed** — no edit to the union, no new ledger row (`error-code-ledger.zod.ts` not in the diff). #9378 holds. `error.message` wording is not touched anywhere; the test matrix uses each door's own wording verbatim.
6. **The #9585 ceiling split.** The ruling relaxes "exactly two keys, no new schema keys" on `/actions` by one named key. In this PR the relaxation is (a) the declared three-key set (pinned by `Object.keys(FlowFailureDetailsSchema.shape)` = `['errorMessage','innerRefusal','summary']`), (b) the `FlowActionRunDetails` docblock in `packages/runtime/src/action-execution.ts:1046-1056` now citing B′ (comment only; the interface still has two fields), while (c) the exact-equality negative pin `actions-flow-dispatch-status.test.ts:377` (`toEqual({ errorMessage, summary })`) is deliberately left. This is a faithful split: the pin asserts what the wire carries today, and nothing emits `innerRefusal` until #24914; relaxing the pin now would weaken a negative pin with no positive emission to replace it, which the ruling does not ask of the spec seat. The split is explicit in the PR body and the dev report, and #24914's claim must own the pin change (flag below). Reviewer choice 2 (declaring `errorMessage`/`summary` beside the new key, so the ceiling is a declared set) accepted: it is what "declare that member ONCE … so the four doors emit one shape" requires, and those two keys already rode the wire undeclared.
7. **Generated artefacts** are consistent with the two new exports: `api-surface`, `export-origins`, `declaration-map`, `authorable-surface`, `json-schema.manifest`, `content/docs/references/{api/automation-api.mdx,index.mdx}` (1542 → 1544, api 438 → 440), strictness ledger `api/` 446 → 448 (two new non-strict object sites). Counts agree with each other.
8. **Tests** (`automation-api.zod.test.ts:547-650`): positive and negative legs for each of the four doors through `BaseResponseSchema` + `FlowFailureDetailsSchema` (+ `ResumeFailureDetailsSchema` on resume), optional-absent leg, three-key pin, closed-code refusal, both-members-required, trigger-data mirror. Matches the card's "what done looks like".
9. **Check-runs on the head** at review time (40 runs): 30 completed, all `success` or `skipped`; none red. Still `in_progress`: Test Core 1-6, Build Core, Type Check · workspace, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · consumer gates. Green already: `Type Check · source gates`, every Lint job incl. `Lint & Repo Gates`, Build Docs, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Spec property liveness. The dev's local red on runtime `check:test-typecheck` (untouched `organization-ownership-boot-guard.turso-remote.kernel.test.ts`) is not reproduced by any red run on this head so far; this PR's runtime diff is a docblock, so it cannot move that verdict. No red run ⇒ no FAIL on this axis; the merge-group guard reads the final state.

### ② Semver level

`@objectstack/spec` **minor**, `Clause-②: yes (widening)` — correct. Two new exported schemas and types, two new optional members on an exported interface and its Zod mirror, every new member optional; an envelope without them parses as before. Nothing narrowed: no enum member removed, no key made required, no message wording moved. The changeset (`.changeset/24996-flow-failed-inner-refusal.md`) names the ruling, the relaxed ceiling and the unchanged channels.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Reviewer choice 1 (closed `ErrorCode` on `innerRefusal.code`)** — accepted. Carrier of the consequence: #24914 (services/cli emission). The emitter must map an inner refusal to the wire member the same way the doors do (`demotedDeclaredCode` / `ThrownHttpError.code` in `packages/types/src/thrown-http-error.ts`); an unregistered hook spelling is demoted and its verbatim form is not carried inside the member. If that spelling turns out to matter to the console, it is a new widening (a `declaredCode` arm on `FlowInnerRefusal`) that needs its own ruling, not a quiet edit.
- **Reviewer choice 2 (declare `errorMessage`/`summary` beside the new key)** — accepted; the declared set is the ceiling now.
- **#9585 runtime pin** — `packages/runtime/src/actions-flow-dispatch-status.test.ts:377` must be relaxed in the same change that emits `innerRefusal`, and the two-door drift pin at `:380` must then cover the third key. Carrier: #24914. Not filed here.
- **Card premise** — the issue body places `AutomationResult` at `automation/flow.zod.ts:1085`; it is `contracts/automation-service.ts`. Carrier: the card's author seat; the dev declared the surface addition in the PR body, which is the correct handling.
- **Runtime `check:test-typecheck` local red** on an untouched file — carrier: CI `Type Check` on this head; not attributable to this diff. Reported above as not red at review time.
- No gate weakened, no held file touched (`dispatcher-plugin.ts`, `crud-nodes.ts`, `engine.ts`, `contract.zod.ts` all untouched).

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-24996-flow-failed-inner-refusal`
Reviewed-by: `session_01D6F9axfoPzR7t8G1J7Ytzz`

**VERDICT: PASS**

**Seat re-read of the check-runs at landing:** all 42 runs on `22786c992e` have completed: 36 succeeded, the rest were skipped, and none is red.
